title: Optimized capacity playbook and utilization dashboard for Dedicated fleets
creator: Ava Thompson
description: Create an actionable playbook and a first-class Grafana dashboard that drive right-sizing recommendations for Dedicated GPU fleets. Deliverables: (1) a Sizing Playbook with heuristics for capacity commitments and recommended autoscaler policies (target utilization, headroom knobs, warm pool sizes, scale cooldowns), (2) a Fleet Utilization dashboard surface showing per-pool and per-customer utilization, 95/99 latency bands, effective cost/unit-token, and projected savings from resizing, and (3) an automated report generator that emits weekly resizing recommendations and an approval flow for sales/CS to accept changes. This ticket scopes the analysis, dashboard prototypes, heuristics, simulation runs, and a staged rollout plan for automated recommendations.
acceptance_criteria: Sizing Playbook doc published in Confluence with explicit heuristics for GPU families and workload mixes
Grafana dashboard panels for pool-level avg/median/95 utilization, per-GPU token throughput, prefix cache hit ratio, and tail-latency by model variant
Weekly recommendation job that produces candidate actions (shrink/grow/keep) with estimated monthly cost delta and predicted P95 latency delta
Manual approval workflow exists (Slack + Console link) before any automated reconfiguration is applied
Simulation tests show <= 3% increase in P95 latency for recommended downsizes under 7-day historical workload traces
implementation_notes: We will reuse existing telemetry (prom: redwood_runtime_gpu_utilization, redwood_runtime_tokens_per_second, redwood_cache_hit) and extend with new derived metrics: effective_cost_per_1k_tokens, padded_headroom_ratio. Autoscaler knobs proposed: target_utilization_percent, max_oversubscription_ratio, warm_pool_min_gpus, scale_down_cooldown_s, scale_up_cooldown_s. Start with read-only dashboard and weekly pull report (manual) before enabling any autoscale actions. Primary concern: avoid oscillation when model rollouts create transient spikes; add a transient spike filter (reject recommendations with >20% variance during peak windows).
work_breakdown: Discovery: review customer commit tiers and historical pool utilization (2d)
Design: draft playbook heuristics and recommended default knobs (3d)
Telemetry: add derived metrics to metrics pipeline and validate (4d)
Dashboard: build Grafana panels and annotation layers (3d)
Simulator: run 7/14/30 day replay sims for candidate changes (5d)
Automation: weekly recommendation job + manual approval flow (5d)
Rollout & Monitoring: pilot with 2 low-risk pools and measure impact (ongoing)
Docs & Training: sales/CS runbook for accepting recommendations (2d)
notes_and_tradeoffs: Tradeoff: aggressive downsizing yields larger cost savings but increases risk of tail-latency regressions during bursty traffic. We favor conservative initial thresholds (target_util 65-75%) and gradual steps (<=20% capacity change per week).
Tradeoff: warm pools increase cost but reduce cold-start latency; propose warm_pool_min = 1-2 GPUs for small pools and 5% of capacity for large pools.
Decision: defer autoscale actions that affect enterprise customers with SLA flags until stakeholder approval. Recommendation engine must surface SLA-tagged pools.
Open: GPU family-sensitive heuristics required; T4 versus A10G versus H100 have different kernel packing behavior — modeling error tolerated up to +/-10% in cost forecasts initially.
sim_results_summary: Ran replay simulations over a 7-day production trace for three candidate pools. Conservative shrink recommendations (10-15% capacity reduction) estimated median monthly savings of ~22% for the pilot pools with simulated P95 latency impact <=2.1%. Aggressive path (25-40% shrink) showed 35-40% savings but introduced up to 8% P95 regressions for model-heavy workloads. Full simulation artifacts attached in Confluence.
